sections.s-hero: Welcome to the Talent Marketplace, Vanderbilt's home for your growth and development. Over the next fifteen minutes we will cover what the marketplace is, the ways in, the process from everyday growth to a landed move, the promises that make it all safe, and your own plan. Stay at Vanderbilt. Go somewhere new. Let's begin.
sections.s-charge: We start with the why. Vanderbilt's charge is bold: define the great university of the twenty-first century, and be it. Three areas of focus make that real: exceptional core operations, bold strategic initiatives, and values leadership. Every one of them runs on talent. When our people grow, the university grows, and that is exactly what the marketplace is for. Dare to grow.
sections.s-what: So what is the Talent Marketplace? Two things, one marketplace. The first is careers of interest, the long game. Name where you want to grow, build toward it, and see openings before the public does. The second is short projects in other units, the short game. They stretch your skills while your home job stays yours. Both live in Oracle, both stay private until you act, and leaders only ever see group totals. When you are ready, test yourself with fact or fiction; most people are surprised by at least one answer.
sections.s-entrances: Now make it personal. There are six doors into the marketplace, and they group into three kinds of talent. Looking to grow: the curious, the plateaued, and the ready. Hidden talent: great in the role, with skills the role never asks for. And not a fit but right mission: after a reorg, or when a role is at risk. Your situation might be a mix, and every door opens the same way: a growth conversation with your manager. Open each door, walk the path inside, and pick the one closest to where you are today.
sections.s-process: The process has two beats, and it is simpler than most people expect. Every day, you build: keep your skills honest and current, flag your careers of interest, and take learning tied to your goals. Then, when opportunity arises, you pursue it: staff see eligible openings first, the interviews are fair, and a chosen move ends with a planned handoff. Growth is daily, and readiness is the reward. Try calling the next move to see how each moment plays out in order.
sections.s-culture: Now the culture work, and this matters most if you lead people. The research is clear: about three out of four managers admit to holding on to strong team members, and that pressure stops people from moving inside. So the promises are plain. No retaliation, ever. No watching. And managers coach. The model response is: thank you for telling me, what drew you to it, and how can I help you prepare well? Releasing talent is a leadership win. The university keeps the skills, and your record shows the development. Take the five manager responses and decide which build the culture and which break it. When you can hear the difference, you are ready to make your plan.
sections.s-plan: Time to make it yours. Five small moves, in order. Have a growth conversation with your manager about your growth and development. Build a plan with the Talent Marketplace tool. Update your career preferences in Oracle. Keep your skills current and honestly leveled. And flag your careers of interest in the Grow area. Each move is small, each link opens the real screen in Oracle, and the printable job aid carries all five with you. Start today.
sections.s-recap: Before we close, a quick check that the big ideas landed. Six questions with instant feedback. Answer honestly, read the why behind each answer, and see how much stuck. Most people are surprised by at least one.
sections.s-close: Let us close with the whole story in one breath. The Talent Marketplace is Vanderbilt's home for your growth and development: identify where you want to grow, build the skills with your manager's support, and pursue opportunities inside the university when they arise. Your activity stays private until you act, and the promises protect you the whole way. Your one next step: a conversation with your manager about your growth and development. Schedule it this week. Thank you for spending fifteen minutes on your future here. Now go grow.
